claims.statement_id: Pada 1789 Christfried Ganander dalam Mythologia Fennica menggambarkan Syöjätär sebagai demon perempuan, setengah demon atau setengah troll, pemakan daging yang kejam dan kanibal ("pemakan manusia").
claims.quote: In 1789, Christfried Ganander described Syöjätär in Mythologia Fennica as a female demon, half-demon or half troll, a cruel flesh-eater and a cannibal ("eater of men").

claims.statement: The lizard is called Syöjätär's brooch, and the snake was born of Syöjätär's spit.
claims.statement_id: Kadal disebut bros Syöjätär, dan ular lahir dari ludah Syöjätär.
claims.quote: The lizard is called the brooch of Syöjätär, and the snake was born out of Syöjätär's spit.

claims.statement: Syöjätär may be a memory of the good-and-bad-creator dualism of Finno-Ugric origin myths and has been compared to the Sámi Áhčešeatni, whose corpse turns into frogs, toads and other unpleasant animals; in fairy tales she is often killed at the end and snakes and other unpleasant animals come from her corpse.
claims.statement_id: Syöjätär bisa dilihat sebagai kenangan mitos dualisme pencipta baik dan buruk dalam mitos asal-usul Fino-Ugria, dan dibandingkan dengan Áhčešeatni Sami yang jasadnya menjadi katak, kodok, dan hewan tak menyenangkan lain; dalam dongeng ia sering dibunuh pada akhir cerita dan dari jasadnya muncul ular dan hewan tak menyenangkan lainnya.
claims.quote: Syöjätär could be seen as a memory of those myths and has been compared to Sámi Áhčešeatni, whose corpse turns into frogs, toads, and other unpleasant animals. In fairytales involving Syöjätär, she is often killed at the end, and snakes and other unpleasant animals come from her corpse.

claims.statement: Cows used to have bellies full of teats, but because Syöjätär complained of having to milk so much, God reduced their number, leaving less milk.
claims.statement_id: Dahulu perut sapi penuh puting, tetapi karena Syöjätär mengeluh harus memerah terlalu banyak, Tuhan mengurangi jumlahnya sehingga susu pun berkurang.
claims.quote: Cows used to have their stomachs full of teats, but as Syöjätär complained about having to milk so much, God reduced the number of them, also resulting in less available milk.

claims.statement: One song tells of Syöjätär's own origin: she came to be when Louhi gave birth to the Nine Diseases and a tenth child, a daughter.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah lagu menceritakan asal-usul Syöjätär sendiri: ia lahir ketika Louhi melahirkan Sembilan Penyakit dan anak kesepuluh, seorang putri.
claims.quote: One song also describes the origin of Syöjätär herself: she came to be when Louhi gave birth to the Nine diseases and a tenth child, a daughter.

claims.statement: In the song "Kuninkaan prinsessa ja Syöjätär" (King's Princess and Syöjätär), Syöjätär casts a spell turning a princess into a blind, mute syöjätär and herself into the princess's likeness.
claims.statement_id: Dalam lagu "Kuninkaan prinsessa ja Syöjätär" (Putri Raja dan Syöjätär), Syöjätär menyihir seorang putri menjadi syöjätär yang buta dan bisu, dan mengubah dirinya agar tampak seperti sang putri.
claims.quote: In the song Kuninkaan prinsessa ja Syöjätär 'King's Princess and Syöjätär', Syöjätär casts a spell, turning a princess into a blind and mute syöjätär, and herself to look like the princess.

claims.statement: The princess regains her form, and she and her brother heat a sauna and lure Syöjätär inside; Syöjätär falls into a deep trap pit and the sauna is set alight, burning her in the pit.
claims.statement_id: Sang putri kembali ke wujud aslinya, lalu ia dan saudaranya memanaskan sauna dan memancing Syöjätär masuk; Syöjätär jatuh ke lubang jebakan dalam dan sauna dibakar sehingga ia terbakar di lubang itu.
claims.quote: The princess got her own form back and the siblings warm up a sauna where they lure Syöjätär into. Syöjätär falls into a deep trap pit and the sauna is set on fire, burning her into the pit.

claims.statement: In folk poetry and fairy tales Syöjätär is an evil female being; the word can also mean a seductress, a "man-eater".
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi rakyat dan dongeng, Syöjätär adalah makhluk perempuan jahat; kata ini juga bisa berarti penggoda, perempuan "penelan lelaki".
claims.quote: Syöjätär on kansanrunoudessa ja saduissa paha naisolento. Syöjätär voi tarkoittaa myös viettelijätärtä, miestennielijää.

claims.statement: In Finnish mythology and folk tradition the syöjätär is an evil spirit.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi dan tradisi rakyat Finlandia, syöjätär adalah roh jahat.
claims.quote: Suomalaisessa mytologiassa ja kansanperinteessä syöjätär on paha henki.

claims.statement: In Elias Lönnrot's collection Suomen kansan muinaisia loitsurunoja, syöjätär is an evil spirit or witch who can be used in conjurations, mentioned alongside other evil spirits such as Hiisi, Perkele and Louhi.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kumpulan Suomen kansan muinaisia loitsurunoja susunan Elias Lönnrot, syöjätär adalah roh jahat atau penyihir yang bisa dipakai dalam mantra pengusiran, dan disebut bersama roh jahat lain seperti Hiisi, Perkele, dan Louhi.
claims.quote: Elias Lönnrotin kokoamassa teoksessa Suomen kansan muinaisia loitsurunoja syöjätär on paha henki tai noita, jota voidaan käyttää manattaessa. Syöjätär mainitaan muiden pahojen henkien, kuten Hiiden, Perkeleen ja Louhen kanssa.

claims.statement: Uriaș is the common Romanian word for giants, who are prominent figures of Romanian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Uriaș adalah sebutan umum dalam bahasa Rumania untuk raksasa, tokoh penting dalam cerita rakyat Rumania.
claims.quote: is the common Romanian-language designation of giants, who are prominent figures in Romanian folklore.

claims.statement: The uriași are figures of myth or fairy tale with human faces, huge, brawny and strong, several fathoms tall, with a stride as long as a post-stage and heads as big as a grain measure; they can chat from one mountain to another and can grab the handles of the sky.
claims.statement_id: Uriaș adalah tokoh mitologi atau dongeng berwajah manusia, besar, kekar, dan perkasa, setinggi beberapa depa, dengan langkah sejauh satu pos perjalanan dan kepala sebesar takaran gandum; mereka bisa mengobrol dari satu gunung ke gunung lain dan mampu berpegangan pada pegangan langit.
claims.quote: Uriașii sunt figuri de mitologie sau basm, cu chip de om, mari, vânjoși, voinici, înalți de mai mulți stânjeni, cu pasul de o de poștă, cu capul cât trei ocale domnești sau mare cât o baniță. Ei pot sta la taifas de la un munte la altul, fiind în stare să se apuce cu mâinile de toartele cerului.

claims.statement: Sometimes they are described as cyclopes with a single eye in the forehead, feeding on human flesh.
claims.statement_id: Kadang mereka digambarkan sebagai kiklops bermata satu di dahi yang memakan daging manusia.
claims.quote: Uneori sunt descriși ca ciclopi, cu un singur ochi în frunte și hrănindu-se cu carne de om.

claims.statement: A common tale tells of an uriaș child who brings home a man with his plough and oxen in his palm like toys, and the parents prophetically explain the passing of their own kind and its replacement by tiny beings; in parts of Oltenia and Transylvania the uriași are also called Jidovi or Novaci.
claims.statement_id: Sering ada kisah anak uriaș yang membawa pulang seorang manusia beserta bajak dan lembunya di telapak tangan seperti mainan, lalu orang tuanya meramalkan punahnya bangsa mereka yang akan digantikan makhluk-makhluk kecil; di beberapa daerah Oltenia dan Transilvania, uriaș juga disebut Jidovi atau Novaci.
claims.quote: De asemenea, e frecvent tipul de poveste în care copilul de Uriaș care aduce acasă în palmă (sau poală) un om cu plugul cu boi, ca pe niște jucării, iar părinții îi explică divinatoriu pieirea propriei stirpe și înlocuirea ei cu ființe mărunte. În unele zone din Oltenia și Transilvania Uriașii se mai numesc și Jidovi sau Novaci.

claims.statement: The uriași are also known as giants said to have built prehistoric forts and earth mounds.
claims.statement_id: Uriaș juga dikenal sebagai raksasa yang konon membangun benteng-benteng prasejarah dan gundukan tanah.
claims.quote: Uriașii sunt cunoscuți și ca giganți care ar fi construit cetățile preistorice și movilele de pământ.

claims.statement: In the lands beyond the Carpathians, the mounds attributed to the uriași, said to have carried earth in their laps, are man-made, burial tumuli of the Bronze and Iron Ages.
claims.statement_id: Di daerah di luar Karpatia, gundukan yang dikaitkan dengan uriaș, yang konon mengangkut tanah dengan pangkuannya, sebenarnya buatan manusia, yaitu tumulus pemakaman dari Zaman Perunggu dan Besi.
claims.quote: În ținuturile extracarpatice movilele puse pe seama Uriașilor, care ar fi cărat pământul cu poala, sunt de origine antropomorfă, tumuli funerari din Epocile Bronzului și Fierului.

claims.statement: A ved is a mythological being recorded in the Bilogora region of northern Croatia, chiefly among speakers of the Kajkavian dialect; the vedi (plural) were described as male humanlike creatures as tall as a peasant house, covered in hair.
claims.statement_id: Ved adalah makhluk mitologis yang tercatat di wilayah Bilogora, Kroasia utara, terutama di kalangan penutur dialek Kajkavia; vedi (bentuk jamak) digambarkan sebagai makhluk lelaki mirip manusia setinggi rumah petani yang seluruh tubuhnya berbulu.
claims.quote: A ved is a mythological being recorded in the region of Bilogora in northern Croatia, predominantly among the region's speakers of the Kajkavian dialect. The vedi (plural) were described as male human-like creatures as high as a peasant house, completely covered with hair.

claims.statement: They were very strong, able to uproot trees and carry heavy loads, with chests so large they could raise storms by blowing; when they spoke or sang they were heard far away.
claims.statement_id: Mereka sangat kuat, mampu mencabut pohon dan memikul beban berat, dan dada mereka begitu besar sehingga tiupannya bisa menimbulkan badai; suara mereka saat berbicara atau bernyanyi terdengar sampai jauh.
claims.quote: They were very strong, able to uproot trees and carry heavy loads, while their chest was so large that they could make storms by blowing. When they spoke or sang, it was heard far away.

claims.statement: There were good and bad vedi; the bad ones shunned people and stayed in their forests, hence the name forest vedi; normally harmless, but a bad ved meeting a young man in the forest would take him to its town and keep him as a slave for a while.
claims.statement_id: Ada vedi baik dan buruk; vedi buruk tidak bergaul dengan manusia dan tinggal di hutan, sehingga disebut vedi hutan; biasanya mereka tak mencelakai orang, tetapi bila bertemu pemuda di hutan, ved buruk akan membawanya ke kotanya dan menjadikannya budak untuk sementara.
claims.quote: There were good and bad vedi. The latter did not associate with people and stayed in their forests, because of which they were also called the forest vedi. They normally did no harm to people, but if a bad ved encountered a young man in a forest, he would take him to his town and keep him as a slave for some time.

claims.statement: The good vedi visited people and helped with daily work or troubles; each household had its own ved, so devoted that it often harmed other households and their vedi.
claims.statement_id: Vedi baik mengunjungi manusia dan membantu pekerjaan sehari-hari atau kesulitan mereka; setiap rumah tangga punya ved sendiri yang sangat setia, sering sampai mencelakai rumah tangga lain beserta vedi mereka.
claims.quote: The good vedi visited people and helped them in their everyday work or troubles. Each household had its own ved who was very devoted to it, often to the extent that he did harm to other households and their vedi.

claims.statement: Facing a flood, storm or other calamity, people prayed that God would let their vedi help them and others' vedi do them no harm; stories say the vedi then came quickly to the rescue.
claims.statement_id: Bila menghadapi banjir, badai, atau bencana lain, orang berdoa agar Tuhan mengizinkan vedi mereka menolong dan vedi orang lain tidak mencelakai; menurut cerita, vedi segera datang menolong setelah doa itu.
claims.quote: If people expected a flood, storm, or other calamity, they would pray, "Grant, Oh God, that our vedi help us!" or "Dear God, grant that our vedi help us, and that their vedi do no harm to us!" Stories have it that after such prayers the vedi would quickly come to rescue.

claims.statement: The last accounts of vedi visiting people date from the mid-19th century, and in the end only certain individuals could supposedly see them.
claims.statement_id: Kisah terakhir tentang vedi yang mengunjungi manusia berasal dari pertengahan abad ke-19, dan pada akhirnya konon hanya orang tertentu yang bisa melihat mereka.
claims.quote: Last accounts of vedi visiting people date from the mid 19th century. In the end only certain individuals were allegedly able to see them.

claims.statement: The Swedish Wikipedia article says that the vedi are said to have been souls of old grandparents.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Wikipedia berbahasa Swedia menyebut bahwa konon vedi adalah jiwa para kakek-nenek yang telah lama meninggal.
claims.quote: Det sägs att det var själar från gamla farföräldrar.

claims.statement: Vitore is a household divine serpent of Albanian mythology and folklore, linked with human destiny, good fortune and the souls of the ancestors; in folk belief the household serpent is closely tied to the cult of the hearth (vatër) and is above all the guardian of the family and house.
claims.statement_id: Vitore adalah ular ilahi penjaga rumah dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Albania, terkait dengan nasib manusia, keberuntungan, dan jiwa para leluhur; dalam kepercayaan rakyat ular rumah ini erat dengan pemujaan perapian (vatër) dan terutama dianggap pelindung keluarga dan rumah.
claims.quote: is a household divine serpent (gjarpër or bollë) in Albanian mythology and folklore, associated with human destiny, good fortune and the souls of the ancestors. In folk beliefs the household serpent is strongly related to the cult of the hearth (vatër) and it is especially considered the guardian of the family and the house.

claims.statement: The name Vitore has been analysed as descending from Albanian vejtare > vektare > vek/vegj, "loom", thus meaning "a woman who spins", linked to the weaving of fate.
claims.statement_id: Nama Vitore ditafsirkan berasal dari kata Albania vejtare > vektare > vek/vegj, "alat tenun", sehingga berarti "perempuan pemintal", terkait dengan menenun nasib.
claims.quote: The name Vitore has been analyzed as descendant from the Albanian vejtare > vektare > vek /vegj , "loom", thus meaning "a spinster, a woman who spins", related to the weaving of fate.

claims.statement: The serpent is an animal totem of the Albanians, especially in the north, and the belief that ancestral souls are personified in household serpents has come down from prehistoric times.
claims.statement_id: Ular adalah totem hewan orang Albania, terutama di utara, dan kepercayaan bahwa jiwa leluhur menjelma dalam ular rumah diwariskan sejak zaman prasejarah.
claims.quote: The serpent is an animal totem of the Albanians, especially in the north. The belief of the personification of the souls of the ancestors in household serpents has been handed down from prehistoric times.

claims.statement: Vitorja is usually described as a small, colourful, benign golden-horned serpent, but in some traditions also as an old woman similar to Nëna e Vatrës; she is also identified with Fatia in southern folklore and Ora in central and northern folklore.
claims.statement_id: Vitorja biasanya digambarkan sebagai ular kecil berwarna-warni yang baik hati dan bertanduk emas, tetapi dalam sebagian tradisi juga sebagai perempuan tua mirip Nëna e Vatrës; ia juga disamakan dengan Fatia dalam folklor selatan dan Ora dalam folklor tengah dan utara.
claims.quote: Vitorja is usually described as a small, colourful and benign golden horned serpent. However, in some traditions Vitorja is described also as an old woman, a mythological figure similar to Nëna e Vatrës. Vitorja is also identified with Fatia in southern folklore and Ora in central and northern folklore.

claims.statement: The household serpent cult appears in Albanian traditional art: a snake silhouette is often carved on house walls and doors for good fortune and against the evil eye.
claims.statement_id: Pemujaan ular rumah tampak dalam seni tradisional Albania: siluet ular sering diukir di dinding dan pintu rumah untuk keberuntungan dan penangkal mata jahat.
claims.quote: The cult of the household serpent is implemented in the Albanian traditional art: the snake silouhette commonly appears carved on the walls and doors of Albanian houses for good fortune and to ward off the evil eye.

claims.statement: As a serpent, when Vitorja lives in a house's walls she is believed to bring luck, so the household treats her with great respect, and her whispering announces important family events.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai ular, bila Vitorja tinggal di dinding rumah ia dipercaya membawa keberuntungan sehingga penghuni memperlakukannya dengan sangat hormat, dan desisannya menandakan peristiwa penting bagi keluarga.
claims.quote: Si gjarpër, kur Vitorja banon në muret e një shtëpie, besohet se sjell fat, kështu që banorët e trajtojnë me shumë respekt. Pëshpëritja e saj lajmëron ngjarje të rëndësishme për familjen.

claims.statement: Valasen (Polish Włosień) is a demonic being of Belarusian mythology found only in the Vileyka district of Minsk Oblast.
claims.statement_id: Valasen (bahasa Polandia: Włosień) adalah makhluk demonik dari mitologi Belarus yang hanya dikenal di distrik Vileyka, Oblast Minsk.
claims.quote: Włosień (biał. "Валасень") – istota demoniczna z mitologii białoruskiej, zlokalizowana tylko w rejonie wilejskim obwodu mińskiego.

claims.statement: It is a small shaggy household demon with large seven-fingered clawed paws; at night it poked and scratched sleeping men until they bled, and the wounds it made healed slowly and festered.
claims.statement_id: Ia demon rumah kecil berbulu lebat dengan cakar besar bertujuh jari; pada malam hari ia menyodok dan mencakar lelaki yang tidur hingga berdarah, dan luka yang ia buat lama sembuh serta bernanah.
claims.quote: To mały, kudłaty demon domowy z wielkimi, siedmiopalczastymi łapami zakończonymi pazurami. Nocami szturchał i drapał do krwi śpiących mężczyzn. Rany zadane przez włosienia długo się goiły i ropiały.

claims.statement: It also frightened children by hissing in their ears and tickling the soles of their feet, groped women in their sleep, and hair grew wherever it touched.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga menakuti anak-anak dengan mendesis di telinga dan menggelitik telapak kaki mereka, meraba perempuan yang sedang tidur, dan di tempat yang ia sentuh tumbuh rambut.
claims.quote: Straszył też dzieci, sycząc im do ucha i łaskocząc je w podeszwy stóp, a kobiety obmacywał podczas snu. W miejscach przez niego dotkniętych wyrastały włosy.

claims.statement: In folk belief Valasen is a house spirit that disturbs and frightens people in their sleep at night; its behaviour resembles the Domovik and other sleep-terrifying beings such as Mara or Nachnitsa.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat, Valasen adalah roh rumah yang setiap malam mengganggu dan menakuti orang yang tidur; perilakunya mirip Domovik dan makhluk mitos penakut orang tidur seperti Mara atau Nachnitsa.
claims.quote: Валасень — у народных павер’ях хатні дух які па начах трывожіць і пужае людзей у сне. У сваіх паводзінах ён нагадвае Дамавіка, а таксама тых міфічных істот, якія пужаюць людзей у сне. Напрыклад Мара ці Начніца.

claims.statement: Valasen is imagined as a small ugly creature covered in thick, long dark fur, with seven-fingered hands and long claw-like nails, walking upright like a person.
claims.statement_id: Valasen dibayangkan sebagai makhluk kecil buruk rupa berbulu gelap yang lebat dan panjang, bertelapak tangan tujuh jari dengan kuku panjang seperti cakar, dan berjalan tegak seperti manusia.
claims.quote: Валасень уяўляецца невялікай пачварнай істотай, парослай густой і доўгай цёмнай поўсцю. Ён таксама мае сяміпалыя далоні і доўгія пазногці-кіпцюры. Ходзіць Валасень, як і людзі, выпрастаўшыся.

claims.statement: According to the Belarusian Wikipedia article, the Valasen tickles men's noses and scratches their faces with his claws, and tangles the hair of women and girls.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel Wikipedia berbahasa Belarus, Valasen menggelitik hidung laki-laki dan mencakar wajah mereka dengan cakarnya, serta mengusutkan rambut perempuan dan gadis.
claims.quote: Мужчынам Валасень казыча насы і драпае кіпцюрамі па твары. Жанчынам і дзяўчатам ён кудлаціць валасы

claims.statement: Kaduk is a marsh spirit, one of the chief evil spirits of Belarusian mythology and the personification of epilepsy.
claims.statement_id: Kaduk adalah roh rawa, salah satu roh jahat utama dalam mitologi Belarus dan personifikasi penyakit epilepsi.
claims.quote: Кадук — балотны дух; у беларускай міфалогіі адзін з галоўных злых духаў, персаніфікацыя хваробы эпілепсіі.

claims.statement: Its name comes from the Latin name of the disease, caducus, "falling".
claims.statement_id: Namanya berasal dari nama Latin penyakit itu, caducus, "yang jatuh".
claims.quote: Сваё імя атрымаў ад лацінскай назвы хваробы caducus — «падучы».

claims.statement: It lives in the darkest forest, in the boggiest marsh, served by lesser unclean spirits; there it judges them and from there sends them to harm people.
claims.statement_id: Ia tinggal di hutan paling gelap, di rawa paling becek, dengan roh-roh najis yang lebih kecil sebagai pelayannya; di sana ia menghakimi mereka dan dari sana ia mengutus mereka mencelakai manusia.
claims.quote: Жыве ў самым цёмным лесе, да таго ж у самым багністым балоце. Тут у яго на службе знаходзяцца меншыя нячысцікі. Тут Кадук чыніць над імі расправу; адсюль жа ён пасылае іх шкодзіць людзям.

claims.statement: Belarusians believe Kaduk eats small children brought to it by its subordinate spirits, driving whole families to extinction.
claims.statement_id: Orang Belarus percaya Kaduk memakan anak-anak kecil yang dibawakan roh-roh bawahannya, sehingga suatu keluarga bisa punah.
claims.quote: Беларусы вераць, што Кадук есць маленькіх дзяцей, якіх яму носяць падначаленыя духі, чым прыводзіць той ці іншы род да вымарачнасці.

claims.statement: By other accounts Kaduk is a beast with a huge shaggy head and a throat wide right up to its ears, gleaming white teeth and a fire-red tongue, seemingly ready to swallow a person whole.
claims.statement_id: Menurut keterangan lain, Kaduk adalah binatang berkepala besar berbulu lebat dengan kerongkongan lebar sampai ke telinga, gigi putih berkilat, dan lidah merah menyala, seolah siap menelan manusia bulat-bulat.
claims.quote: Па іншых звестках Кадук — звер з вялізарнай калматай галавой і шырокім горлам аж да самых вушэй. У яго пашчы блішчаць белыя зубы і чырванее, як агонь, язык, і здаецца, што ён гатовы праглынуць чалавека цалкам, з касцямі і патрахамі.

claims.statement: Belarusians held that without the limits on when it can appear, Kaduk would long since have seized everyone; and if someone wishes, at just such an evil moment, that Kaduk take another person, the curse will come true.
claims.statement_id: Orang Belarus menganggap bahwa tanpa batasan waktu kemunculannya, Kaduk sudah lama menculik semua orang; dan bila seseorang mengutuk orang lain agar diambil Kaduk tepat pada saat sial itu, kutukan itu akan terwujud.
claims.quote: Калі б не гэтыя абмежаванні, то Кадук, лічылі беларусы, даўно пахапаў бы ўсіх людзей. І, калі нехта менавіта ў такі ліхі момант пажадае, каб іншага чалавека ўзяў Кадук, то праклён здзесніцца.

claims.statement: The Ukrainian article calls Kaduk the oldest of the forest spirits and demons, living deep in the darkest forest in a sticky bog.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Ukraina menyebut Kaduk sebagai roh dan demon hutan tertua yang tinggal di kedalaman hutan paling gelap di rawa lengket.
claims.quote: найстаріший з лісових духів та демонів що живе в глибині самого темного лісу в в'язкому болоті.

claims.statement: In Belarusian folklore Khabyor is the king of all crayfish, recognisable by his golden claws and eyes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam folklor Belarus, Khabyor adalah raja semua udang karang, yang bisa dikenali dari capit dan matanya yang keemasan.
claims.quote: Хабёр — у беларускім фальклоры цар усіх ракаў, якога можна было пазнаць па залатых клюшнях і вачах.

claims.statement: In magic tales he is the hero's magical helper, ordering the crayfish to find a ring lost in the sea.
claims.statement_id: Dalam dongeng ajaib ia penolong gaib sang pahlawan, yang memerintahkan udang-udang karang mencari cincin yang hilang di laut.
claims.quote: У чарадзейных казках — чароўны памочнік героя, які загадвае ракам знайсці ў моры згублены пярсцёнак.

claims.statement: The Ukrainian article calls him a lake spirit, the oldest crayfish, king and patron of all crustaceans and protector of the whole lake realm, with huge golden claws and eyes, who also helps people find things lost in the water.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Ukraina menyebutnya roh danau, udang karang tertua, raja dan pelindung semua krustasea serta penjaga seluruh kerajaan danau, bercapit dan bermata emas besar, yang juga membantu orang menemukan barang yang hilang di air.
claims.quote: персонаж білоруської міфології, озерний дух — найстаріший рак, цар й покровитель усіх ракоподібних, а також захисник всього озерного царства. Він володіє величезними золотими клешнями та очима. Хабйор також допомагає людям знайти їх загублені в воді речі.

claims.statement: In Belarusian mythology Pyachurnik is a spirit living in or behind the stove; it looks like a cat but walks on its hind legs and avoids being seen, and like the domovik it is the guardian of the house it lives in; as a mark of respect the housewife set out supper leftovers or milk on the stove at night.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Belarus, Pyachurnik adalah roh yang tinggal di dalam atau di belakang tungku; rupanya mirip kucing tetapi berjalan dengan kaki belakang dan berusaha tidak menampakkan diri, dan seperti domovik ia pelindung rumah tempat tinggalnya; sebagai penghormatan, nyonya rumah menaruh sisa makan malam atau susu di atas tungku pada malam hari.
claims.quote: Пячурнік — у беларускай міфалогіі дух, які жыве ў печы ці за печчу. Абліччам нагадвае ката, толькі ходзіць на задніх лапах, чалавеку стараецца не паказвацца. З’яўляўся, як і дамавік, апекуном таго дома, дзе жыў. У знак пашаны гаспадыня выстаўляла ноччу на печы пачастунак пячурніку — рэшткі вячэры альбо малако.

claims.statement: In the Ukrainian article, the Pichnyk (like the domovyk) is the guardian of the household hearth, always in, on or behind the stove.
claims.statement_id: Dalam artikel Ukraina, Pichnyk (seperti domovyk) adalah penjaga perapian rumah yang selalu berada di dalam, di atas, atau di belakang tungku.
claims.quote: Пічник (як і домовик) — охоронець домашнього вогнища. Він постійно перебуває в печі, на печі чи за нею.

claims.statement: If not treated with due attention, the pyachurnik, from sorrow, revenge or offence, will howl and shout in the chimney and rattle the damper for several nights in a row.
claims.statement_id: Bila tidak diperlakukan dengan perhatian semestinya, pyachurnik karena sedih, dendam, atau tersinggung akan melolong dan berteriak di cerobong serta menggerakkan penutup cerobong dengan berisik selama beberapa malam berturut-turut.
claims.quote: Калі ж да яго паставяцца без належнай увагі, пячурнік ад суму, помсты ці крыўды будзе некалькі начэй запар выць і крычаць у коміне, грукатаць уюшкаю.

claims.statement: Having the ability to foresee trouble and unpleasantness, he starts moving furniture and knocking down and breaking dishes to warn the householders.
claims.statement_id: Karena mampu meramalkan bencana dan kesulitan, ia mulai menggeser perabot serta menjatuhkan dan memecahkan peralatan makan untuk memperingatkan para pemilik rumah.
claims.quote: Маючы здольнасць прадбачыць бяду і непрыемнасці, пачынае пасоўваць мэблю, скідваць і разбіваць посуд — каб папярэдзіць гаспадароў.

claims.statement: But the pyachurnik is also inclined to joke: he carries a needed item away from its usual place and hides it.
claims.statement_id: Namun pyachurnik juga suka bercanda: ia memindahkan barang yang diperlukan dari tempat biasanya dan menyembunyikannya.
claims.quote: Але пячурнік схільны і пажартаваць: зносіць патрэбную рэч са звычнага месца і хавае яе.

claims.statement: Folklorists recorded belief in the pyachurnik in the Maladzechna area.
claims.statement_id: Para ahli folklor mencatat kepercayaan pada pyachurnik di wilayah Maladzechna.
claims.quote: Фалькларысты зафіксавалі веру ў пячурніка на Маладзечаншчыне.

claims.statement: According to the Ukrainian article on his counterpart, the pichnyk, when the family goes to sleep he is busy with sweeping the stove, the hearth ledge and the floor carefully.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel Ukraina tentang padanannya, pichnyk, ketika keluarga tidur ia sibuk menyapu tungku, tepi tungku, dan lantai dengan cermat.
claims.quote: Коли родина лягає спати, тоді для нього безліч клопотів: дбайливо замести піч, припічок і долівку

claims.statement: According to the same article, if the housewife is tidy the pichnyk helps her with housework; for a careless woman he can make the soot in the stove begin to smolder, or even cause a fire.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel yang sama, jika nyonya rumah rapi, pichnyk membantunya dalam pekerjaan rumah; pada perempuan yang ceroboh ia bisa membuat jelaga dalam tungku mulai membara, bahkan menyebabkan kebakaran.
claims.quote: Якщо господиня охайна, пічник допомагає їй у хатній роботі. Непутящій жінці може зробити так, що сажа в печі почне тліти, а то й спричинить пожежу.

claims.statement: Among the Russian population of the north of European Russia, the Kama region, the Urals, Siberia and the Far East, shulikuny is the name of the unclean beings of Sviatki: seasonal spirits that come out of the water onto land before Christmas or New Year and go back into rivers and ice-holes after Epiphany.
claims.statement_id: Pada penduduk Rusia di utara Rusia Eropa, Prikamye, Ural, Siberia, dan Timur Jauh, shulikuny adalah nama makhluk najis masa Sviatki: roh musiman yang menjelang Natal atau Tahun Baru keluar dari air ke darat dan setelah Hari Epifani kembali ke sungai dan lubang es.
claims.quote: — у русского населения севера Европейской части России, Прикамья, Урала, Сибири, Дальнего Востока название святочной нечисти — сезонных духов, которые накануне Рождества или Нового года выходят из воды на землю, а после Крещения уходят обратно в реки и проруби.

claims.statement: According to belief, shulikuny run through the streets with hot coals in an iron pan or a red-hot iron hook with which they can catch people ("hook and burn"), or ride horses, troikas, mortars or "red-hot" stoves.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan, shulikuny berlarian di jalan membawa bara panas di wajan besi atau kait besi membara untuk menangkap orang ("mengait dan membakar"), atau menunggang kuda, kereta troika, lesung, atau tungku yang membara.
claims.quote: Согласно поверьям, шуликуны бегают по улицам с горячими углями на железной сковородке или железным калёным крюком в руках, которым они могут захватить людей («закрючить и сжечь»), либо ездят на конях, на тройках, на ступах или «калёных» печах.

claims.statement: They are often fist-sized, sometimes larger, may have horse legs and a pointed head (compare the devil), and fire blazes from their mouths.
claims.statement_id: Mereka sering sebesar kepalan tangan, kadang lebih besar, bisa berkaki kuda dan berkepala runcing (bandingkan setan), dan dari mulut mereka menyala api.
claims.quote: Ростом они нередко с кулачок, иногда побольше, могут иметь конские ноги и заострённую голову (ср. Чёрт), изо рта у них пылает огонь

claims.statement: In Vologda belief, babies cursed or killed by their mothers become shulikuny.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan di Vologda, bayi-bayi yang dikutuk atau dibunuh ibunya menjadi shulikuny.
claims.quote: По вологодским представлениям, шуликунами становятся проклятые или погубленные матерями младенцы.

claims.statement: In Ukrainian mythology the shulikuny are mythical beings born on Christmas Eve in stove chimneys who go under the water at Epiphany.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Ukraina, shulikuny adalah makhluk mitos yang lahir pada Malam Natal di cerobong tungku dan masuk ke bawah air pada Hari Epifani.
claims.quote: Шулікуни — міфічні істоти, персонажі української міфології. Ці істоти народжуються на Святвечір в коминах печей і йдуть під воду на Водохреща.

claims.statement: With the hot hook they can catch a drunken man, spin him round, push him into the mud, even lure him into an ice-hole.
claims.statement_id: Dengan kait membara itu mereka bisa menangkap lelaki pemabuk, memutar-mutarnya, mendorongnya ke lumpur, bahkan memikatnya ke lubang es.
claims.quote: якою можуть захопити чоловіка-п’яницю: крутять його, штовхають у багнюку, можуть навіть в проруб заманити.

claims.statement: In Belarusian mythology the loyma is a spirit in the form of a beautiful girl; loymas live in forests and marshes and are a threat to people.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Belarus, loyma adalah roh berwujud gadis cantik; loyma tinggal di hutan dan rawa dan berbahaya bagi manusia.
claims.quote: у беларускай міфалогіі дух у прыгожым дзявочым абліччы. Лоймы жывуць у лясах і балотах і прадстаўляюць пагрозу для людзей.

claims.statement: In the book "Lud białoruski na Rusi Litewskiej" M. Federowski writes that loymas are evil spirits in female form, living mostly in marshes and frightening village women, sometimes men too; they have long tangled hair and are frightful.
claims.statement_id: Dalam buku "Lud białoruski na Rusi Litewskiej", M. Federowski menulis bahwa loyma adalah roh jahat berwujud perempuan yang paling sering tinggal di rawa dan menakuti perempuan desa, kadang juga lelaki; rambut mereka panjang dan kusut dan rupa mereka mengerikan.
claims.quote: У кнізе «Люд беларускі на Русі Літоўскай» М. Федароўскі піша, што лоймы — злыя духі ў жаночым абліччы. Жывуць найчасцей у балотах і страшаць вясковых жанчын, хаця часам пужаюць і мужыкоў. У лоймаў доўгія раскудлачаныя валасы, а самі яны страшныя.

claims.statement: By contrast, according to Mikola Haiduk's records, loymas are very beautiful girls who meet mortal men in the forest and caress them.
claims.statement_id: Sebaliknya, menurut catatan Mikola Haiduk, loyma adalah gadis-gadis yang sangat cantik yang menemui lelaki fana di hutan dan membelai mereka.
claims.quote: Паводле запісаў Міколы Гайдука, лоймы, насупраць, вельмі прыгожыя дзяўчыны. Яны спаткаюць у лесе смяротных мужчын, лашчаць іх

claims.statement: They appeared only to those who burned charcoal deep in the forest.
claims.statement_id: Mereka hanya menampakkan diri kepada orang yang membakar arang di kedalaman hutan.
claims.quote: Сустракаліся яны толькі тым, хто выпальваў вугаль у лясных нетрах.

claims.statement: According to the Ukrainian article, she most often appears as an ugly woman of medium height with a green body, long tangled hair, ordinary hands but enormous feet.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel Ukraina, ia paling sering tampil sebagai perempuan buruk rupa bertinggi sedang, bertubuh hijau, berambut panjang kusut, bertangan biasa tetapi berkaki luar biasa besar.
claims.quote: Найчастіше постає у вигляді огидної жінки середнього зросту, з зеленим тілом, з довгим розплатаним волоссям, звичайними руками, але з неймовірно великими ногами.

claims.statement: She mostly pesters young girls and also steals children from their mothers, leaving her own misshapen offspring in their place.
claims.statement_id: Ia terutama mengganggu gadis muda dan juga mencuri anak dari ibunya, menggantinya dengan anaknya sendiri yang cacat.
claims.quote: В основному чіпляється до молодих дівчат, а також викрадає дітей у матерів, підкидаючи замість них своїх виродків

claims.statement: Kudava (Moksha kud, Erzya kudo "house"; ava "woman") is a pre-Christian Mordvin deity, protectress of the house, believed to live under the stove, the threshold, beneath the floor or in the front corner of the house.
claims.statement_id: Kudava (Moksha kud, Erzya kudo "rumah"; ava "perempuan") adalah dewi pra-Kristen orang Mordvin, pelindung rumah, yang dipercaya tinggal di bawah tungku, ambang pintu, ruang bawah lantai, atau sudut depan rumah.
claims.quote: Кудава (м. куд, э. кудо «дом», м., э. ава «женщина») — дохристианское божество мордвы, покровительница дома. Считали, что Кудава обитает под печью, порогом, в подполье, переднем углу дома.

claims.statement: Later the Moksha and some Erzya used the Turkic word "yurt" for the house with all its outbuildings, and the house deity was called Yurtava.
claims.statement_id: Kemudian orang Moksha dan sebagian Erzya memakai kata Turkik "yurt" untuk rumah beserta bangunan pekarangannya, dan dewi rumah itu disebut Yurtava.
claims.quote: Позднее для обозначения дома со всеми надворными постройками мокша и часть эрзи стали применять тюркское слово «юрт» и божество дома названное Юртавой.

claims.statement: When building a house, horse, cow, sheep or goat hair was laid under the first logs on the posts sunk into the ground so the house would last, and a table was set with bread, salt and wine.
claims.statement_id: Saat membangun rumah, bulu kuda, sapi, domba, atau kambing diletakkan di bawah balok pertama di atas tiang yang ditanam agar rumah awet, dan meja disiapkan dengan roti, garam, dan anggur.
claims.quote: При строительстве жилища под первые брёвна на столбах, вкапываемых в землю, клали шерсть лошади, коровы, овцы или козы, чтобы дом был долговечным. При этом накрывали стол, ставили на него хлеб, соль, вино.

claims.statement: The custom of putting animal hair and money in a house's foundation shows that in the past there were real, not symbolic, sacrifices to the house deity.
claims.statement_id: Kebiasaan meletakkan bulu hewan dan uang di fondasi rumah menunjukkan bahwa dahulu ada kurban nyata, bukan sekadar simbolis, bagi dewi rumah.
claims.quote: Обычай класть в основание дома шерсть животного и деньги говорит о том, что в старину были не символические, а реальные жертвоприношения божеству дома.

claims.statement: In Erzya: Kudava is the guardian of the house, and the word Kudava is formed from two words, "kudo" and "ava".
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Erzya: Kudava adalah penjaga rumah, dan kata Kudava terbentuk dari dua kata, "kudo" dan "ava".
claims.quote: Кудава — кудонь ванстыця. Кудава валось теевсь кавто валтнэнь эйстэ — «кудо» ды «ава».

claims.statement: According to the article, people believed that in such a case Kudava would assist them in all their affairs and their home would prosper.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel itu, orang percaya bahwa dalam kasus demikian Kudava akan membantu mereka dalam segala urusan dan rumah mereka akan sejahtera.
claims.quote: Люди верили, что Кудава в таком случае окажет им содействие во всех делах и в их доме будет благополучие.

claims.statement: According to the article, Kudava is mentioned in spells, prayers, wedding songs and laments.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel itu, Kudava disebut dalam mantra, doa, lagu pernikahan, dan ratapan.
claims.quote: Кудаву упоминают в заговорах, молитвах, свадебных песнях и причитаниях.

claims.statement: According to N. I. Kostomarov, Dana is a water goddess of Slavic mythology, patroness of rivers, streams and waters; modern scholarship considers the hypothesis mistaken.
claims.statement_id: Menurut N. I. Kostomarov, Dana adalah dewi air dalam mitologi Slavia, pelindung sungai, anak sungai, dan perairan; ilmu modern menganggap hipotesis ini keliru.
claims.quote: — по мнению Н. И. Костомарова, богиня воды в славянской мифологии, покровительница рек, ручьев и водоёмов. Современной наукой гипотеза признана ошибочной.

claims.statement: Kostomarov supported his conclusion with river names such as the Dvina, Danube (Dunai), Don and Dnieper (Danapris) and the refrain "dana, dana" in ritual songs.
claims.statement_id: Kostomarov mendasarkan kesimpulannya pada nama-nama sungai, seperti Dvina, Danube (Dunai), Don, dan Dnieper (Danapris), serta refrein "dana, dana" dalam lagu-lagu ritual.
claims.quote: Свой вывод он аргументирует, приводя названия рек: Двина, Дунай, Дон, Днепр (Данаприс) и припев в обрядных песнях: дана, дана.

claims.statement: Kostomarov wrote of Dana: "like water, the beginning of things, eternally beautiful, eternally fresh, she was a maiden and at the same time a wife, that is, the consort of the sun."
claims.statement_id: Kostomarov menulis tentang Dana: "seperti air, awal segala sesuatu, abadi jelita, abadi segar, ia adalah perawan sekaligus istri, yaitu permaisuri matahari."
claims.quote: О Дане Костомаров пишет: «как вода, начало вещей, вечно прекрасная, вечно свежая, она была дева и вместе жена, то есть супруга солнца».

claims.statement: The Ukrainian article calls Dana a hypothetical water goddess of Slavic mythology, patroness of rivers, streams and waters, possibly also named Divanna, Divoniya or Diva.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Ukraina menyebut Dana dewi air hipotetis dalam mitologi Slavia, pelindung sungai, anak sungai, dan perairan, yang mungkin juga bernama Divanna, Divoniya, atau Diva.
claims.quote: — гіпотетична богиня води в слов'янській міфології, покровителька річок, струмків і водойм. Також її іменами можуть бути Діванна, Дівонія, Діва.

claims.statement: Danylo Lepky, in his study of spring customs and beliefs in Rus, wrote that all the rusalkas obey one eldest lady, whom the common people in their tales simply call "Diva", "Divka", "Divchyna" or "Dana".
claims.statement_id: Danylo Lepky dalam kajian tentang adat dan kepercayaan musim semi di Rus menulis bahwa semua rusalka mematuhi seorang nyonya tertua, yang oleh rakyat dalam cerita-cerita mereka disebut "Diva", "Divka", "Divchyna", atau "Dana".
claims.quote: Данило Лепкий у розвідці «Весняні звичаї, обряди та віруваня на Руси» писав ... Всї Русалки слухають одної найстаршої панї, котру простий люд в своїх оповіданях називає просто «Діва», «Дівка», «Дівчина» або «Дана».

claims.statement: In Kostomarov's own text, the most important names for the female water being among the Slavs were Devoniya, Dzevanna and Dana.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tulisan Kostomarov sendiri, penamaan terpenting bagi makhluk perempuan-air di kalangan bangsa Slavia adalah Devoniya, Dzevanna, dan Dana.
claims.quote: Но важнейшею из номинаций женско-водного существа у славян была Девония, Дзеванна и Дана.

claims.statement: Kostomarov wrote that among the Eastern Slavs she probably bore, besides Mokosh, the name Dana and simply Deva, as shown by some place and water names, for example "devyi gory", "devichye pole" and the river "Devitsa".
claims.statement_id: Kostomarov menulis bahwa di kalangan Slavia Timur ia mungkin, selain Mokosh, juga bernama Dana dan sekadar Deva, seperti ditunjukkan beberapa nama tempat dan perairan, misalnya "devyi gory", "devichye pole", dan sungai "Devitsa".
claims.quote: у нас она, вероятно, кроме Мокошь, имела еще название Дана, и просто Дева, как это показывают некоторые урочища и названия вод, напр., девьи горы, девичье поле, река девица.

claims.statement: According to the modern view in the article, the names Deva and Devoniya on which Kostomarov relies are not names of some separate female deity but epithets of Mokosh.
claims.statement_id: Menurut pandangan modern dalam artikel itu, nama Deva dan Devoniya yang dijadikan dasar oleh Kostomarov bukan nama dewi perempuan yang terpisah, melainkan julukan Mokosh.
claims.quote: Имена Дева, Девония, к которым апеллирует Костомаров, стремясь обосновать свои построения, не являются именами какого-то отдельного женского божества, в действительности это эпитеты Мокоши.

claims.statement: In Belarusian mythology Zhaleznaya baba (Iron Hag) is an evil spirit used to frighten children.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Belarus, Zhaleznaya baba (Nenek Besi) adalah roh jahat yang dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak-anak.
claims.quote: Жалезная баба - у беларускай міфалогіі злы дух, якім пужалі дзяцей.

claims.statement: She lives in the garden or field, a wicked short old woman with iron breasts; children who go into the garden or field without their parents' permission she catches with an iron hook, throws into her iron mortar, pounds and then eats.
claims.statement_id: Ia tinggal di kebun atau ladang, berupa nenek tua jahat bertubuh pendek dengan payudara besi; anak-anak yang pergi ke kebun atau ladang tanpa izin orang tua ia tangkap dengan kait besi, dilempar ke lesung besinya, ditumbuk, lalu dimakan.
claims.quote: Жыве ў агародзе ці ў полі. Злая старая бабка нізенькага росту, з жалезнымі грудзямі. Дзяцей, якія без дазволу бацькоў ходзяць у агарод ці ў поле, яна хапае жалезным круком, кідае ў сваю жалезную ступу, таўчэ там, а потым з'ядае.

claims.statement: According to the ethnographer Shakhovich, in other parts of Belarus she was believed to live in a well and to pull in children who peered into it.
claims.statement_id: Menurut etnograf Shakhovich, di daerah lain di Belarus orang percaya Zhaleznaya baba tinggal di sumur dan menarik masuk anak-anak yang mengintip ke dalamnya.
claims.quote: Паводле звестак этнографа Шаховіча, у іншых мясцінах Беларусі верылі, быццам Жалезная баба жыве ў студні. Дзяцей, якія заглядаюць у студню, яна ўцягвае да сябе.

claims.statement: The Ukrainian article notes that she bears some resemblance to the Rusalka and Baba Yaga.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Ukraina menyebut bahwa ia memiliki kemiripan tertentu dengan Rusalka dan Baba Yaga.
claims.quote: Вона, також, має певну схожість з Русалкою та Бабоюю-Ягою.

claims.statement: According to the Ukrainian article, she most often appears as a repulsive little old woman with shaggy, disheveled hair and huge iron breasts.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel Ukraina, ia paling sering tampil sebagai nenek buruk rupa bertubuh kecil dengan rambut kusut dan dada besi yang besar.
claims.quote: Найчастіше постає у вигляді огидної бабки невеликого зросту, з кошлатими розпатланим волоссям й величезними залізними грудьми.

claims.statement: The article says she always carries an iron hook, a mortar and a pestle, with which she catches and pounds any disobedient children she has caught.
claims.statement_id: Artikel itu menyebut ia selalu membawa kait besi, lumpang, dan alu yang dipakainya untuk menangkap dan menumbuk anak-anak nakal yang tertangkap.
claims.quote: Завжди носить з собою залізний гак, ступку й товкач, якими вона ловить та дробить всіх спійманих неслухняних дітей.

claims.statement: According to the article, she sometimes torments children before killing them, by strangling, drowning and other means; besides killing, she may also simply frighten them.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel itu, kadang ia menyiksa anak-anak sebelum membunuh mereka, dengan mencekik, menenggelamkan, dan cara lain; selain membunuh, ia juga bisa sekadar menakut-nakuti mereka.
claims.quote: Часом, вона мучить дітей перед вбивством — душить їх, топить, і знущається іншими способами. Однак, крім вбивства дітей — може й просто налякати їх.

claims.statement: Zwodziasz, also called zwodzijos (in Sieradz), is a devilish creature of Slavic mythology said to lead people astray and lure them into wasteland until they lose their way, often indirectly causing their sudden death.
claims.statement_id: Zwodziasz, juga disebut zwodzijos (di Sieradz), adalah makhluk setan dalam mitologi Slavia yang konon menyesatkan orang dan memikat mereka ke tanah tandus hingga tersesat, sering secara tak langsung menyebabkan kematian mendadak mereka.
claims.quote: Zwodziasz, known also as zwodzijos (Sieradz), is a diabolic creature in Slavic mythology. It was said to lead people astray and decoy them into wasteland, making them lose their way and often indirectly becoming the cause of their sudden death.

claims.statement: In tales of people from Kalisz and its surroundings, the zwodziasz is portrayed as a nightjar.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita orang dari Kalisz dan sekitarnya, zwodziasz digambarkan sebagai burung cabak (nightjar).
claims.quote: In tales of people from Kalisz and its vicinity, zwodziasz is portrayed as a nightjar.

claims.statement: Afruvvá (from Norwegian havs fru, "lady of the sea") is a being known mainly among the coastal Sami of the Finnmark (Ruija) coast, representing a relatively young storytelling tradition shared with the Scandinavians.
claims.statement_id: Afruvvá (dari bahasa Norwegia havs fru, "nyonya laut") adalah makhluk yang terutama dikenal di kalangan Sami pesisir di pantai Finnmark (Ruija), mewakili tradisi cerita yang relatif muda dan dimiliki bersama orang Skandinavia.
claims.quote: Afruvvá (< norjan havs fru, 'meren rouva') on lähinnä Ruijan rannikon merisaamelaisten parissa tunnettu olento, joka edustaa saamelaisten parissa nuorta, skandinaavien kanssa yhteistä kertomusperinnettä.

claims.statement: Afruvvá is a typical mermaid, a beautiful long-haired, fish-tailed woman who appears at sea.
claims.statement_id: Afruvvá adalah putri duyung khas: perempuan cantik berambut panjang dan berekor ikan yang menampakkan diri di laut.
claims.quote: Afruvvá on tyypillinen merenneito, kaunis, pitkätukkainen ja kalanpyrstöinen nainen, joka näyttäytyy merellä.

claims.statement: Originally afruvvá was probably a guardian spirit of seafarers who, by appearing to them, urged them to return to shore in time.
claims.statement_id: Awalnya afruvvá tampaknya roh pelindung pelaut yang, dengan menampakkan diri, mendesak mereka kembali ke pantai tepat waktu.
claims.quote: Alun perin afruvvá lienee esiintynyt merenkävijöitä suojelevana haltijana, joka näille näyttäytymällä kehottaa heitä palaamaan ajoissa rantaan.

claims.statement: Sometimes she is also said to capsize boats and cause other trouble, but this seafarer-harassing afruvvá has probably taken on traits of another water spirit of Scandinavian origin, the rávgá, classed among the dead.
claims.statement_id: Kadang ia juga disebut membalikkan perahu dan menimbulkan gangguan lain, tetapi afruvvá pengganggu pelaut ini tampaknya mengambil ciri roh air asal Skandinavia lain, yaitu rávgá yang tergolong arwah orang mati.
claims.quote: Toisinaan hänen kylläkin mainitaan myös kaatavan veneitä ja tuottavan muuta häiriötä, mutta tämä merenkävijöitä ahdisteleva avruvvá lienee saanut toisen skandinaavisperäisen vedenhaltijan, vainajaolentoihin luokiteltavan rávgán piirteitä.

claims.statement: The Saami Cultural Encyclopedia, which the Wikipedia article cites, gives the same description: the afruvvá is a typical mermaid, a beautiful, long-haired, fish-tailed woman who shows herself at sea.
claims.statement_id: Ensiklopedia Kebudayaan Sami (yang dirujuk artikel Wikipedia) memuat uraian yang sama: afruvvá adalah putri duyung tipikal, perempuan cantik berambut panjang dan berekor ikan yang menampakkan diri di laut.
claims.quote: Afruvvá on tyypillinen merenneito, kaunis, pitkätukkainen ja kalanpyrstöinen nainen, joka näyttäytyy merellä.

claims.statement: The encyclopedia supposes that the afruvvá originally appeared as a guardian spirit of seafarers who, by showing itself to them, urged them to return to shore in good time.
claims.statement_id: Ensiklopedia itu menduga afruvvá semula tampil sebagai roh pelindung para pelaut yang, dengan menampakkan diri kepada mereka, mendesak mereka kembali ke pantai tepat waktu.
claims.quote: Alun perin afruvvá lienee esiintynyt merenkävijöitä suojeleva haltijana, joka näille näyttäytymällä kehottaa heitä palaamaan ajoissa rantaa.

claims.statement: Anki-Kiele (also Anky-Kele, Anka-Kal; Chukchi "spirit of the sea") is the sea spirit of Chukchi and Eskimo mythology.
claims.statement_id: Anki-Kiele (juga Anky-Kele, Anka-Kal; bahasa Chukchi: "roh laut") adalah roh laut dalam mitologi Chukchi dan Eskimo.
claims.quote: (также Анкы-Келе, Анка-Кал; чук. «дух моря») — дух моря в чукотской и эскимосской мифологии.

claims.statement: Anki-Kiele belongs to the kele spirits, a category including not only forces hostile to people but also master spirits (aun-ralyt).
claims.statement_id: Anki-Kiele termasuk golongan roh kele, yang mencakup bukan hanya kekuatan yang memusuhi manusia, tetapi juga roh-roh penguasa (aun-ralyt).
claims.quote: Анки-Киеле относится к категории духов-келе, которая включает в себя не только враждебные человеку силы, но и духов-хозяев (аун-ральыт).

claims.statement: According to a drawing by the Chukchi artist Onno (1912–1953), Anki-Kiele lives on the sea bed and has a huge shaggy head with two eyes and a large toothy maw.
claims.statement_id: Menurut gambar seniman Chukchi Onno (1912–1953), Anki-Kiele tinggal di dasar laut dan berkepala besar berbulu dengan dua mata dan mulut lebar bergigi.
claims.quote: Согласно рисунку чукчи Онно (1912—1953), Анки-Киеле живёт на дне моря, имеет огромную мохнатую голову с двумя глазами и большой зубастой пастью.

claims.statement: A drawing from V. G. Bogoraz's collection shows Anki-Kiele with the body of a fish.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah gambar dari koleksi V. G. Bogoraz menggambarkan Anki-Kiele bertubuh ikan.
claims.quote: Рисунок из собрания В. Г. Богораза ... изображает Анки-Киеле с телом рыбы.

claims.statement: Anki-Kiele could grant a good catch of fish or success in hunting other sea creatures, which could be obtained by sending a shaman's soul to him.
claims.statement_id: Anki-Kiele bisa memberikan tangkapan ikan yang baik atau keberhasilan berburu hewan laut lain, yang bisa diupayakan dengan mengirim jiwa seorang dukun (shaman) kepadanya.
claims.quote: Анки-Киеле мог послать хороший улов рыбы или успех в добыче прочих морских обитателей. Этого можно было добиться, послав к нему душу шамана.

claims.statement: Bogoras records a "spirit" living in the sea (a'nqa-kal), pictured with the body of a fish and a very large shaggy head.
claims.statement_id: Bogoras mencatat sebuah "roh" yang hidup di laut (a'nqa-kal) yang digambarkan bertubuh ikan dengan kepala berbulu yang sangat besar.
claims.quote: a “spirit” living in the sea (a'nqa-kal), has the body of a fish, with a very large shaggy head.

claims.statement: On another sketch Bogoras describes a large sea-spirit with very long hair on both his head and his buttocks.
claims.statement_id: Pada sketsa lain, Bogoras menyebut roh laut besar yang berambut sangat panjang di kepala dan pantatnya.
claims.quote: On another sketch is represented a large sea-spirit, who has very long hair on both his head and his buttocks.

claims.statement: Babaroga is a being of South Slavic mythology once used to frighten children; she is often confused with the witch, although they are different mythological beings.
claims.statement_id: Babaroga adalah makhluk dari mitologi Slavia Selatan yang dulu dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak-anak; ia sering dicampuradukkan dengan penyihir, meskipun keduanya makhluk mitologis yang berbeda.
claims.quote: Бабарога је биће из митологије Јужних Словена. Њом су се некада плашила дјеца. Бабарога се често мијеша са вјештицом, иако су то различита митолошка бића.

claims.statement: In folk tradition she is described only as a frightening female being, a hunched, ugly, toothless old woman with a deformed face and a horn on her head (from which she takes her name), who hides in dark places and comes out only at night, frightening and snatching naughty children away to her lair.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi rakyat ia digambarkan semata-mata sebagai makhluk perempuan menakutkan berupa nenek bungkuk, buruk rupa, ompong, berwajah cacat, dengan tanduk di kepala (asal namanya), yang bersembunyi di tempat gelap dan hanya keluar malam hari, serta menakuti dan menculik anak-anak nakal ke sarangnya.
claims.quote: У народним предањима се описује искључиво као застрашујуће женско биће у облику погрбљене, ружне, крезубе старице наказног лица са рогом на глави (по коме је и добила име), које се крије на тамним местима и излази само ноћу. Према народним предањима бабарога плаши и отима неваљалу дјецу, и одводи их у свој брлог.

claims.statement: The Baba Yaga article lists Baba Roga among related figures, used to scare children in Bosnia, Croatia, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia.
claims.statement_id: Artikel tentang Baba Yaga menyebut Baba Roga sebagai tokoh Serbia yang dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak-anak di Bosnia, Kroasia, Montenegro, Makedonia Utara, dan Serbia.
claims.quote: Baba Roga (used to scare children in Bosnia, Croatia, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia)

claims.statement: In Serbian, Croatian, Macedonian, Romanian and Bulgarian, baba means "grandmother" or "old woman".
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Serbia, Kroasia, Makedonia, Rumania, dan Bulgaria, baba berarti "nenek" atau "perempuan tua".
claims.quote: In Serbian, Croatian, Macedonian, Romanian and Bulgarian, baba means 'grandmother' or 'old woman'.

claims.statement: The Serbian Wikipedia article on Baba Yaga says witches are also considered successors of the Slavic goddess Morana, who was portrayed with a horn, flew on a broom and sailed on an eggshell.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Wikipedia berbahasa Serbia tentang Baba Yaga menyebut bahwa penyihir dianggap pewaris dewi Slavia Morana, yang digambarkan dengan tanduk, terbang dengan sapu, dan berlayar di cangkang telur.
claims.quote: Такође се сматра да су вештице наследнице словенске богиње Моране, која је представљана са рогом, летела на метли и пловила на љусци од јајета

claims.statement: The article adds that Baba Roga, Baba Ruga, Baba Kozma and Baba Yaga could have arisen from her description.
claims.statement_id: Artikel itu menambahkan bahwa dari penggambaran Morana itu mungkin muncul Baba Roga, Baba Ruga, Baba Kozma, dan Baba Yaga.
claims.quote: Из њеног описа могле су произаћи Баба Рога, Баба Руга, Баба Козма и Баба Јага.

claims.statement: The Croatian Wikipedia article on Baba Jaga lists Baba Roga among the names of a figure who in Slavic mythology is a witch, sorceress or forest spirit.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Wikipedia berbahasa Kroasia tentang Baba Jaga memasukkan Baba Roga sebagai salah satu nama tokoh yang dalam mitologi Slavia disebut penyihir, tukang sihir, atau roh hutan.
claims.quote: Baba Jaga, Baba Roga, Ježi-babo ili Baba Zima u slavenskoj mitologiji vještica je, čarobnica ili šumski duh.

claims.statement: Božalość, also transliterated Božaloshtsh or Bozaloshtsh, is a messenger of misfortune or death in Wendish mythology (the Wends, Lusatian Sorbs).
claims.statement_id: Božalość, juga ditulis Božaloshtsh atau Bozaloshtsh, adalah pembawa kabar kemalangan atau kematian dalam mitologi Wend (orang Sorbia Lusatia).
claims.quote: Božalość, also transliterated as Božaloshtsh or Bozaloshtsh is a messenger of misfortune or death in Wendish mythology (Wends, Lusatian Sorbs).

claims.statement: In German ethnographic sources the name was translated as "Gottesklage", that is, "God's Lament".
claims.statement_id: Dalam sumber etnografi Jerman, namanya diterjemahkan sebagai "Gottesklage", yaitu "Ratapan Tuhan".
claims.quote: The name was translated in German ethnographic sources as "Gottesklage" i.e., "God's Lament").

claims.statement: An 1886 article, Das Spreewaldhaus by W. v. Schulenburg, links it with the elder bush and describes it as a woman in white with long, unkempt hair and red eyes.
claims.statement_id: Artikel tahun 1886 Das Spreewaldhaus karya W. v. Schulenburg mengaitkannya dengan semak elder dan menggambarkannya sebagai perempuan berpakaian putih, berambut panjang kusut, dan bermata merah.
claims.quote: An 1886 article Das Spreewaldhaus by W. v. Schulenburg associates it with the elder bush and describes it as a woman dressed in white with long, unkempt hair and red eyes

claims.statement: Biren Bonnerjea describes it as a little long-haired woman who weeps under the window of someone about to die.
claims.statement_id: Biren Bonnerjea menggambarkannya sebagai perempuan kecil berambut panjang yang menangis di bawah jendela orang yang akan meninggal.
claims.quote: Biren Bonnerjea describes it as a little woman with long hair, who cries under the window of someone who is about to die.

claims.statement: A parallel creature is the bože sedleško, described as a child in white clothes.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk sejajarnya adalah bože sedleško, yang digambarkan sebagai anak berpakaian putih.
claims.quote: A parallel creature is bože sedleško, described as a child in white clothes.

claims.statement: The appearance of a bože sedleško signals coming misfortune: death, fire, epidemics, flood and so on.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan bože sedleško menandakan bencana yang akan datang: kematian, kebakaran, wabah, banjir, dan sebagainya.
claims.quote: An appearance of a bože sedleško manifests a coming misfortune: death, fire, epidemics, flood, etc.

claims.statement: According to Bonnerjea's dictionary, among the Wends she is a messenger of death: a little woman with long hair who cries like a child beneath the window of a house where someone is about to die.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus Bonnerjea, di kalangan bangsa Wend ia adalah pembawa kabar kematian: perempuan kecil berambut panjang yang menangis seperti anak kecil di bawah jendela rumah tempat seseorang akan meninggal.
claims.quote: among the Wends she is a messenger of death. She is a little woman with long hair, who cries like a child, beneath the window of a house where someone is about to die.

claims.statement: Opinions on the etymology differ: some see it as a contraction of "Boža žaloć" ("God's Pity"); others note that the word "Glosc" meaning "lament" appears in manuscripts as early as the 17th century and that the attribute "Boža" ("God's") was added later in folklore.
claims.statement_id: Pendapat tentang asal kata berbeda: ada yang melihatnya sebagai kontraksi "Boža žaloć" ("Belas Kasih Tuhan"); pendapat lain menyatakan kata "Glosc" yang berarti "ratapan" sudah ada dalam naskah abad ke-17 dan sifat "Boža" ("milik Tuhan") ditambahkan kemudian dalam cerita rakyat.
claims.quote: In some opinions it is the contraction of "Boža žaloć", i.e., "God's Pity". Another opinion is that the word "Glosc" in the meaning of "lament" can be found in manuscripts of as early as the 17th century, and the attribute 'Boža' i.e., "God's" was added in folklore later

claims.statement: Brodarica or brodawica is a Serbo-Croatian and Bulgarian Slavic demon, a kind of vila.
claims.statement_id: Brodarica atau brodawica adalah demon Slavia dari tradisi Serbia-Kroasia dan Bulgaria, sejenis vila.
claims.quote: Brodarica, brodawica – serbsko-chorwacki i bułgarski demon słowiański; rodzaj wił.

claims.statement: She had a female form and lived in bodies of water, chiefly fords and shallows, which she guarded against people.
claims.statement_id: Ia berwujud perempuan dan menghuni perairan, terutama arungan dan tempat dangkal, yang ia jaga dari manusia.
claims.quote: Posiadała kobiecą postać, zamieszkiwała zbiorniki wodne – głównie brody i płycizny. Strzegła te miejsca przed człowiekiem.

claims.statement: In Tatar belief, Bunis is a demon subject to Bun, marked by great malice and enormous strength, which attacks together with other Bunises.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan Tatar, Bunis adalah demon bawahan Bun yang sangat jahat dan luar biasa kuat, dan menyerang bersama Bunis lainnya.
claims.quote: Bunis – według wierzeń tatarskich demon podporządkowany Bunowi. Cechuje go wielka złośliwość i olbrzymia siła. Atakuje wraz z innymi Bunisami.

claims.statement: Only a clear conscience protects against them; yet shamans tame them and believe that with their help they can foretell the future.
claims.statement_id: Satu-satunya perlindungan dari mereka adalah hati nurani yang bersih; namun para dukun menjinakkan mereka dan percaya bahwa berkat mereka para dukun dapat meramalkan masa depan.
claims.quote: Chroni przed nimi jedynie czyste sumienie. Jednakże szamani oswajają je i uważają, że dzięki nim potrafią przepowiadać przyszłość.

claims.statement: In Sami storytelling tradition the čáhkalakkis is an underground being the size of a small child living in mountain hollows; among the Skolt Sami its counterpart is the čeäk'kli, among the Kildin and Ter Sami the čahhkli, and among the Inari Sami the tšahalag.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi cerita Sami, čáhkalakkis adalah makhluk bawah tanah seukuran anak kecil yang tinggal di rongga-rongga gunung; padanannya pada orang Sami Skolt disebut čeäk'kli, pada Sami Kildin dan Ter čahhkli, dan pada Sami Inari tšahalag.
claims.quote: Čáhkalakkis on saamelaisessa kertomusperinteessä maanalainen, pikkulapsen kokoinen, vuorien onkaloissa asuva olento. Sitä vastaavat koltansaamelaisilla čeäk'kli, kildinin- ja turjansaamelaisilla čahhkli ja inarinsaamelaisilla tšahalag.

claims.statement: The čáhkalakkis is a benevolent being that appears naked or scantily dressed; these earth-dwellers are a people foreign but not hostile to the Sami, and they speak their own language, which the Sami understand only with difficulty.
claims.statement_id: Čáhkalakkis adalah makhluk baik hati yang tampil telanjang atau berpakaian minim; makhluk bawah tanah ini bangsa yang asing tetapi tidak bermusuhan bagi orang Sami, dan berbicara dengan bahasa sendiri yang sulit dipahami orang Sami.
claims.quote: Čáhkalakkis on hyväntahtoinen olento, joka esiintyy joko alastomana tai vähissä vaatteissa. Nämä maahiset ovat saamelaisille vierasta, mutta eivät vihamielistä kansaa. Ne puhuvat omaa kieltään, jota saamelaiset vaivoin ymmärtävät.

claims.statement: They own various goods, gold and silver, which a person can obtain by a certain trick.
claims.statement_id: Mereka memiliki berbagai barang, emas, dan perak, yang bisa didapat manusia dengan cara tertentu.
claims.quote: Ne omistavat erilaisia tavaroita, kultaa ja hopeaa, joita ihminen voi saada tietyllä konstilla.

claims.statement: To catch the earth-dweller, porridge and a fur shoe with its laces must be set by the hollow as bait.
claims.statement_id: Untuk menangkap makhluk bawah tanah ini, bubur dan sepatu bulu beserta talinya harus diletakkan di dekat rongga sebagai umpan.
claims.quote: Saadakseen maahisen kiinni on asetettava onkalon viereen puuroa sekä karvakenkä pauloineen syötiksi.

claims.statement: When the earth-dwellers ran out of riches they sent people wooden spoons as a sign that they had nothing more to give; one must not take everything from them, because a greedy person's descendants become poor.
claims.statement_id: Ketika harta mereka habis, makhluk bawah tanah itu mengirim sendok kayu kepada manusia sebagai tanda tak ada lagi yang bisa diberikan; orang tak boleh mengambil segalanya dari mereka, karena keturunan orang tamak akan jatuh miskin.
claims.quote: Kun maahisilta loppuivat rikkaudet, ne lähettivät ihmisille puulusikat merkiksi siitä, ettei niillä ole enää mitään annettavaa. Maahisilta ei saanut ottaa kaikkea, koska ahneen ihmisen jälkeläiset köyhtyvät.

claims.statement: The gold-and-silver motif in the čáhkalakkis tradition and its role as a treasure-owning spirit are presumably of Old Scandinavian or even Germanic origin.
claims.statement_id: Motif emas dan perak dalam tradisi čáhkalakkis serta peran sebagai roh pemilik harta diduga berasal dari tradisi Skandinavia kuno atau bahkan Jermanik.
claims.quote: Kulta-hopea -motiivi čáhkalakkis-perinteessä sekä haltija-aarteenomistaja -ulottuvuus ovat otaksuttavasti muinaisskandinaavista tai jopa germaanista alkuperää.
